course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Statistics II: Inferential Statistics and Statistical Modeling
course.description: This course focuses on applying statistical methods in research and decision-making in data science and engineering. This course covers inferential statistics and multivariate analysis, equipping students with the skills to analyse complex datasets. Students will explore topics such as probability, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and multivariate analysis. Emphasis is placed on practical applications, using statistical software to conduct data analysis and interpret results.

topics.title: Topic 1: Hypothesis Testing and p-Value Lab 1: SPSS (Insert, manage, edit, and describe data)
topics.llosRaw: Apply hypothesis testing and p-value to interpret the data in the research process.

topics.title: Topic 2: Confidence Interval and Test of Normality of Data Lab 2: SPSS (Check normality of data)
topics.llosRaw: Apply confidence interval and normality testing to double-check the statistical data in the research process.

topics.title: Topic 3: Dependent and Independent Samples Topic 3: Parametric and Non-parametric Tests Lab 3: SPSS (Data coding, creating variables by computing, and plotting the data)
topics.llosRaw: Distinguish between dependent and independent samples for statistical data analysis. Distinguish between parametric and non-parametric tests for statistical data analysis.

topics.title: Topic 4: One-Sample t-Test Lab 4: SPSS (One-sample t-Test)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison of one independent group with a specified value by a one-sample t-test and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 5: Paired sample t-Test Lab 5: SPSS (Paired Sample t-Test)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison between two dependent groups by a paired sample t-test and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 6: Independent sample t-Test Lab 6: SPSS (Independent Sample t-Test)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison between two independent groups by an independent sample t-test and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 7: One-way ANOVA Lab 7: SPSS (One-way ANOVA)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison of three or more independent groups by the One-way ANOVA and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 8: One-way ANOVA with Repeated Measurement Lab 8: SPSS (One-way ANOVA with repeated Measurement)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison of three or more dependent groups by the One-way ANOVA with repeated measurements and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 9: Two-way ANOVA Lab 9: SPSS (Two-way ANOVA)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison of three or more independent groups by the Two-way ANOVA and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 10: Two-way ANOVA with Repeated Measurement Lab 10: SPSS (Two-way ANOVA with Repeated Measurement)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a parametric test comparison of three or more dependent groups by the Two-way ANOVA with repeated measurements and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 11: Linear regression correlation of bivariate data Lab 11: SPSS (Correlation and regression)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a correlation relationship and regression line modelling between two variables by using the statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 12: Multiple regression analysis Lab 12: SPSS (Multiple regression)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a multiple regression analysis between three or more variables by using the statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 13: Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney U test Lab 13: SPSS (Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney U Test)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a non-parametric test comparison between two groups by the Wilcoxon and Mann-Whitney U test and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

topics.title: Topic 14: Kruskal-Wallis test Lab 14: SPSS (Non-parametric test: Kruskal-Wallis test)
topics.llosRaw: Conduct a non-parametric test comparison of three or more dependent groups by the Kruskal-Wallis test and interpret the results using statistical software SPSS.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
